title: What to Wear for Maternity Photos in the RGV | Adrisabel
description: What to wear for maternity photos: studio gowns, bump-friendly shapes, soft colors and outfits for partners and kids — tips from a McAllen-area studio.
focus: what to wear for maternity photos
h1: What to wear for maternity photos (and what to leave at home)
dek: From studio gowns to comfortable shoes, here’s how to choose outfits that show your bump, suit a soft studio look and bring the whole family together.
intro:
The short answer to what to wear for maternity photos: something that shows the shape of your bump — fitted or softly flowing — in a solid, gentle color and a fabric that drapes. Studio gowns are available too, so you can wear one of those or bring your own favorites.

Since every maternity session happens indoors, in Adrisabel’s private studio in the McAllen area, you can dress for comfort and the camera instead of Rio Grande Valley weather. Below, we’ll go through shapes, colors and fabrics, how to dress your partner and kids, and the small details that make the day easier.

sections.html:
Studio gowns are available for maternity sessions, and they’re often the easiest place to start. Choosing one takes a shopping trip off your list and gives you an elegant look without buying something you may wear only once.

When you reach out, ask about the gowns and mention anything you’re thinking of bringing yourself. Adrisabel helps you plan outfits and colors that feel like you, so whatever you choose works with your partner and kids. You can read more about the session on our maternity photography page.

Still deciding on a date? Our guide on when to take maternity photos covers timing. This one is all about getting dressed.

sections.h2: Pick shapes that show your bump
sections.html:
Your bump is the heart of these portraits, so choose pieces that let its shape show. Two approaches work especially well:

  • Fitted: a stretchy knit or ribbed dress, or a fitted top, that follows the curve of your belly. It’s clean and modern, and the shape reads clearly from every angle.
  • Flowing: a long, soft dress that skims over the bump and falls loosely below it. A wrap style, or a waistline that sits above the bump, keeps the fabric from hiding your shape.

What tends to work less well: boxy tunics, oversized sweaters and stiff layers that cover the bump completely. If you love a cozy cardigan, wear it open over a fitted dress so the curve still shows.

Before the day, sit down in each outfit, lift your arms and walk around the room. If something pulls, pinches or rides up at home, it will bother you during the session too.

sections.h2: Soft, solid colors for a soft studio look
sections.html:
Solid colors keep the attention on you, your bump and the people you love. Gentle tones suit a soft studio look especially well, and they tend to feel timeless when you look back years from now.

  • White, ivory and cream
  • Blush, dusty rose and mauve
  • Sage, soft blue and muted teal
  • Oatmeal, taupe and warm beige

A deeper shade, such as burgundy, olive or navy, can look beautiful on a partner, as long as the overall palette stays calm. If you can’t decide between two colors you love, bring both and talk them through with Adrisabel.

sections.h2: Fabrics that drape — and what to leave at home
sections.html:
Fabric makes more of a difference than most people expect. Pieces that drape, such as jersey, chiffon, soft knits, lace and tulle, fall naturally around the bump and move gently when you turn. Stiff fabrics tend to crease, stand away from the body and blur your shape.

A few things are best left in the closet:

  • Logos and slogans: words pull the eye away from faces.
  • Busy prints: loud patterns, tiny checks and thin stripes can look distracting on camera.
  • Neon and very bright colors: they can reflect color onto skin.
  • Anything untested: try new pieces on, and wash them if needed, well before the day.

Hang or steam everything the night before. Wrinkles are easy to miss at home and hard to miss in a portrait.

sections.h2: Coordinate your partner and kids without matching
sections.html:
Partners and big brothers and sisters are welcome, and dressing everyone is easier than it sounds. Aim for a shared palette rather than identical outfits: pick two or three colors from your own look and let everyone else wear a variation of them.

  • Partner: a solid button-down, a soft knit polo or a fine sweater in a neutral or a deeper shade from your palette. Simple and well fitting beats trendy.
  • Kids: soft solids with a little texture — knit, linen, a cotton dress — and nothing stiff or scratchy that will make them restless.
  • Everyone: a similar level of dressiness. If you’re in a long gown, jeans and a T-shirt beside you will stand out.

A few days before the session, lay all the outfits out together on a bed and take a quick photo with your phone. Anything that jumps out on the screen will jump out in the portraits, too.

sections.h2: Shoes, hair, makeup and a couple of backups
sections.html:
Shoes: wear something comfortable for getting there — flats, sandals or clean sneakers. Feet often swell later in pregnancy, and with a long dress your shoes usually won’t show anyway.

Hair and makeup: as a general tip, choose a polished version of your everyday look rather than something brand new. Matte or satin-finish makeup tends to photograph better than very shiny products. If you’re booking a stylist, a trial run takes away the guesswork.

Hands and jewelry: hands often rest on or around the bump in maternity portraits, so tidy nails in a neutral shade are worth a few minutes. Keep jewelry simple — your rings and one delicate piece are plenty.

Options: bring two or three outfits, steamed and on hangers, with the shoes and accessories for each. If you’re driving in from elsewhere in the Valley — Harlingen is about 40–45 minutes away, Brownsville about 60–70 minutes — hang them in the car rather than folding them into a bag.

Once your maternity outfits are sorted, the next chapter is closer than it feels. If you haven’t already, reserve your newborn session when you book maternity — we’ll save a spot around your due date and set the session within those first 5–14 days.

The good news is that newborn day takes far less wardrobe planning. The studio is stocked with wraps, outfits, bonnets, headbands, little beds, baskets and backdrops in soft, timeless colors, and you’re welcome to bring a meaningful item from home. For a family newborn session, the palette you chose for maternity can carry right over — our guide on what to wear for newborn photos picks up from there.

When you’re ready, ask about maternity portraits and mention your due date. We reply within 24 hours with maternity details and availability, and you can compare the Sunshine and Wonderland sessions on our newborn photography page.

faq.q: Do you have maternity gowns I can wear?
faq.a: Yes, studio gowns are available for maternity sessions. Ask about them when you get in touch, and Adrisabel will help you plan outfits and colors around them.

faq.q: What should my partner wear for maternity photos?
faq.a: Something simple and well fitting in a color that coordinates with yours, such as a solid button-down or a fine knit. Match your level of dressiness, and skip logos and loud prints.

faq.q: Can I wear jeans for maternity photos?
faq.a: Yes, if that feels most like you. Pair them with a fitted top that shows your bump, and keep your partner and kids at the same relaxed level so the look feels intentional.
